title: Incident Metadata Standard (Observability)
author: Allison Grant
body:
h1. Incident Metadata Standard (Observability)

This page defines the *standard incident metadata fields* captured for production incidents at Redwood Inference and the *allowed values* for each field. The purpose is to make incident data consistent enough for:

* fast, low-cognitive-load incident declaration and triage
* ownership clarity and correct paging
* reliable aggregation in dashboards (incident volume, MTTR/TTM, error budget burn correlation)
* trend reporting and prioritization (reliability roadmap input)

This standard is used by:

* the Slack incident-bot declaration modal and status updates
* postmortem templates
* the incident tagging ingestion pipeline feeding SRE datasets + Grafana dashboards

*Non-goals:* This document does not redefine severity, contractual SLAs, or the Security Incident Response (IR) process. Security incidents may reuse select fields but remain governed by Security IR.

h2. Guiding principles

# *Minimal required fields during live response.* We optimize for correctness under pressure.
# *Stable enums.* Allowed values should change rarely; additions are preferred over renames.
# *“Unknown” is allowed.* We must be able to declare an incident quickly even with incomplete information.
# *Two-phase accuracy.* It is acceptable to refine metadata after mitigation, but not acceptable to leave it blank.
# *Reportability.* Fields must map to queryable dimensions used by dashboards.

h2. Field summary (v1)

The following fields are standardized. “Required” means required *by the incident-bot* at declare time or within the specified window.

|| Field key || Display name || Type || Required (declare / within 15 min / postmortem) || Notes ||
| incident.category | Category | single-select enum | within 15 min | Primary classification for reporting and ownership routing. |
| incident.impacted_surface | Impacted surface | multi-select enum | declare | What product/deployment surface(s) are impacted. |
| incident.customer_tier | Customer tier | single-select enum | declare | Highest impacted tier (if multiple, pick highest). |
| incident.region | Region | multi-select enum | declare | Regions materially impacted. Use “global” if broad/unclear. |
| incident.contributing_factors | Contributing factors | multi-select enum | postmortem | Use for trend analysis; does not replace root cause narrative. |

Recommended (strongly encouraged):

* incident.primary_service (free text with conventions below)
* incident.owner_team (single-select from on-call owning teams; derived in tooling where possible)

h2. Field definitions + allowed values

h3. incident.category (single-select)

*Definition:* The best-fit primary incident type based on what is failing. Choose the category that most directly describes the *mechanism* of failure, not the symptom.

*Usage rule:* During live response, pick the closest category and proceed. Reclassify later if needed.

Allowed values (v1):

|| Value || Definition (when to use) || Common examples ||
| routing.overload_or_policy | Smart routing / policy layer is shedding load, misrouting, or enforcing incorrect limits | sudden spike of 429/503 due to routing policy, incorrect model routing, tier-based routing bug |
| capacity.exhaustion_or_autoscaling | Insufficient GPU/CPU capacity or autoscaling behavior causing saturation | dedicated pool saturation, scale-up stuck, fleet insufficient in a region |
| runtime.crash_or_hang | Inference runtime process crashes, deadlocks, or becomes unresponsive | pod crash loops, GPU OOM crash, scheduler hang |
| runtime.performance_regression | Runtime is up but has materially degraded latency/throughput | p95 latency doubles after deploy, batcher regression |
| model.quality_or_output_regression | Output quality/format correctness regresses (not just latency/availability) | structured output breaks, increased refusal/garbage text due to model/version/config |
| gateway.edge_or_streaming | Edge/gateway layer issues affecting request acceptance, streaming, or connectivity | streaming disconnects, websocket issues, gateway timeouts, TLS handshake errors |
| control_plane.deployment_or_config | Control plane, rollout, or config propagation causes incorrect behavior | bad config push, rollout controller stuck, model version pinning failure |
| dependency.upstream_provider | A third-party dependency materially impacts service | cloud region outage, managed DB degradation, external auth outage |
| observability.telemetry_gap | Monitoring/telemetry gaps materially impair detection/triage (may be secondary) | metrics pipeline down, traces missing, alert routing broken |
| data_plane.storage_or_cache | Caching/storage layers impacting inference path | KV cache cluster issues, prefix cache corruption, shared cache timeouts |
| release.rollback_required | A production release is the primary driver; rollback is the mitigation | deploy introduces errors across multiple services, rapid rollback needed |
| other_or_unknown | Use when unsure; must be refined by postmortem | novel failure mode, incomplete info |

Notes:

* If the incident is clearly caused by a release, prefer *release.rollback_required* even if symptoms appear in routing/runtime.
* If a dependency outage is dominant (e.g., cloud region/network failure), use *dependency.upstream_provider*.
* *observability.telemetry_gap* is typically a contributing factor, not the primary category, unless the incident impact is “we were blind and could not operate safely.”

h3. incident.impacted_surface (multi-select)

*Definition:* Which customer-facing surfaces or deployment modes are materially impacted.

Allowed values (v1):

|| Value || Definition / examples ||
| hosted.api | Hosted Redwood API (multi-tenant) request path for chat/completions/embeddings/rerank |
| hosted.streaming | Streaming responses specifically (SSE/websocket) |
| dedicated.pools | Dedicated capacity pools (reserved clusters) |
| private.vpc_or_onprem | Redwood-operated Private deployments (VPC/on-prem) where Redwood is primary operator for day-2 |
| console.ui | Redwood Console UI (dashboards, configuration screens) |
| console.rollouts | Rollouts UI/policies (canary, A/B, fallback configuration) |
| sdk.client_libs | SDKs (Python/TS/etc.) causing customer breakage |
| auth.billing_or_quotas | Auth, billing, quota enforcement, API keys |
| status_page | Status page update path / status visibility |
| internal.ops_tooling | Internal-only operational tooling (incident-bot, on-call tools) |

Selection guidelines:

* Pick all that apply, but avoid “everything.” If unsure, select the surface(s) customers report or monitoring shows.
* If the API is affected and streaming is affected, select both *hosted.api* and *hosted.streaming*.

h3. incident.customer_tier (single-select)

*Definition:* Highest tier of customer impacted (or the tier requiring comms/priority handling). If multiple tiers are impacted, choose the highest.

Allowed values (v1):

|| Value || Meaning ||
| internal_only | No external customer impact; only internal systems / testing |
| self_serve | Self-serve / PLG customers on standard support |
| growth | Paid mid-market customers with business-hours support expectations |
| enterprise | Enterprise customers (contractual SLA language may apply) |
| strategic | Named strategic accounts requiring elevated comms/exec visibility |

Notes:

* If a Dedicated pool for an Enterprise customer is affected, use *enterprise* (or *strategic* if applicable), even if Hosted is unaffected.
* This field is used to determine comms expectations and escalation thresholds in support playbooks.

h3. incident.region (multi-select)

*Definition:* Cloud region(s) where customer impact is observed. Select “global” if impact is cross-region or not yet attributable.

Allowed values (v1):

|| Value || Notes ||
| global | Use when multiple regions are affected or region attribution is unknown early |
| us-east-1 | Primary NA East region |
| us-west-2 | Primary NA West region |
| eu-central-1 | Primary EU region |
| eu-west-1 | Secondary EU region |
| ap-southeast-1 | Primary APAC region |

Guidelines:

* During declaration, it is acceptable to start with *global* and later refine.
* If the incident is Dedicated-only and isolated to a single customer region/pool, select that region rather than global.

h3. incident.contributing_factors (multi-select)

*Definition:* Secondary factors that materially contributed to impact, time-to-mitigate, or recurrence risk. These are used for cross-cutting reliability initiatives.

Allowed values (v1):

|| Value || Examples ||
| deploy_or_change_management | risky deploy window, missing canary, inadequate rollback automation |
| capacity_planning | insufficient headroom, missing forecasts, regional imbalance |
| autoscaling_policy | bad scaling thresholds, scale-to-zero surprises, slow warm-up |
| alerting_gaps | missing alerts, noisy alerts causing fatigue, wrong paging route |
| observability_gaps | missing traces/logs, low-cardinality labels, incomplete dashboards |
| runbook_gap | unclear or outdated mitigation steps |
| ownership_ambiguity | wrong team paged, unclear escalation path |
| config_or_feature_flag | bad config, unreviewed flag changes, config propagation delay |
| dependency_instability | recurring upstream issues, weak failover behavior |
| testing_coverage | missing load tests, missing regression tests, prompt/eval coverage gaps |
| communication_gaps | delayed customer updates, internal coordination issues |
| other | include details in postmortem narrative |

Selection guidelines:

* Contributing factors are not blame. Prefer selecting 1–4 that are clearly supported by the timeline.

h2. Conventions for free-text fields (recommended)

These fields are not strict enums today, but we standardize *format* so they remain queryable.

h3. incident.primary_service (recommended)

Format: *<domain>/<service>* (lowercase, dash-separated). Examples:

* platform/smart-routing
* platform/control-plane
* infra/gpu-fleet-manager
* runtime/scheduler
* gateway/edge-proxy
* obs/metrics-pipeline

Rule: Use the service closest to the failure mechanism, not the surface.

h3. incident.owner_team (recommended / tooling-derived)

In incident-bot and dashboards this is typically derived from category + primary_service via the ownership map. If set manually, use the on-call owning team name exactly as follows:

* SRE
* Platform
* Runtime
* Infra-Fleet
* Networking
* Observability
* Support (for support-process-only incidents)

h2. Mapping to metrics and dashboards

h3. Canonical tag keys in datasets

All ingestion pipelines must emit these keys exactly:

* incident.category
* incident.impacted_surface
* incident.customer_tier
* incident.region
* incident.contributing_factors
* incident.primary_service (recommended)
* incident.owner_team (recommended)

Cardinality constraints:

* *incident.primary_service* is expected to have low cardinality (tens to low hundreds). Do not include instance IDs, pod names, customer IDs, or ticket IDs.
* *incident.contributing_factors* is multi-select but bounded by the enum list.

h3. Metric views (Grafana / reporting)

The following standard aggregations are expected to work across all incident data sources (incident bot, postmortems):

* Incident volume by *incident.category* (weekly/monthly)
* MTTR and TTM by *incident.owner_team* and *incident.category*
* Customer impact slices by *incident.customer_tier* and *incident.impacted_surface*
* Regional heatmaps by *incident.region*
* Contributing factor trends (top factors over 30/90 days)

Naming convention for dashboard variables:

* $category maps to incident.category
* $surface maps to incident.impacted_surface
* $tier maps to incident.customer_tier
* $region maps to incident.region
* $owner maps to incident.owner_team

h3. How metadata affects alerting and routing (operational use)

* incident-bot uses *incident.category* + *incident.primary_service* to suggest *incident.owner_team* and the initial paging route.
* Support escalation playbooks use *incident.category* and *incident.customer_tier* to determine:
  * whether to page SRE/Eng immediately
  * update cadence expectations
  * whether an incident requires an external customer update

h2. Required timing and reclassification rules

h3. During incident declaration

Required at declare time:

* incident.impacted_surface
* incident.customer_tier
* incident.region

Required within 15 minutes:

* incident.category

If unknown, select:

* incident.category = other_or_unknown
* incident.region = global

…but the IC (or delegated Ops lead) must refine within the first hour if evidence becomes available.

h3. After mitigation (postmortem hygiene)

Within the postmortem:

* Confirm or update incident.category
* Add incident.contributing_factors
* Ensure incident.primary_service is set (if the failure is attributable)

If the category changes post-incident:

* Document the change in the postmortem “What changed since declaration?” section.
* Do not delete the original values from the timeline; preserve what was known at the time.

h2. Examples

h3. Example A: Dedicated pool saturation

* incident.category: capacity.exhaustion_or_autoscaling
* incident.impacted_surface: dedicated.pools
* incident.customer_tier: enterprise
* incident.region: us-east-1
* incident.primary_service: infra/gpu-fleet-manager
* incident.contributing_factors: capacity_planning, autoscaling_policy

h3. Example B: Streaming disconnects at the edge

* incident.category: gateway.edge_or_streaming
* incident.impacted_surface: hosted.api, hosted.streaming
* incident.customer_tier: self_serve
* incident.region: us-west-2
* incident.primary_service: gateway/edge-proxy
* incident.contributing_factors: alerting_gaps, runbook_gap

h3. Example C: Bad routing policy change

* incident.category: routing.overload_or_policy
* incident.impacted_surface: hosted.api
* incident.customer_tier: growth
* incident.region: global
* incident.primary_service: platform/smart-routing
* incident.contributing_factors: config_or_feature_flag, deploy_or_change_management

h2. Validation and “allowed values” enforcement

Tooling requirements:

* Incident-bot must enforce the enums exactly as listed in this document.
* Any changes to enums must be coordinated with dashboard owners to avoid breaking saved queries.
* The ingestion pipeline must reject unknown values *unless* they are explicitly listed as “other”/“unknown.”

Operational requirements:

* If an enum value needs to be added, do not repurpose an existing value.
* Avoid renaming values. If a rename is required, add a new value and run a migration/backfill.

h2. Change management

This standard is treated as an *observability contract*.

To propose changes:

# Open a change request (Linear) with justification (impact on reporting/ops).
# Update this page + incident-bot enums + dashboards in the same rollout window.
# If the change is material (new top-level categories, merging/splitting), record an ADR.
# Communicate rollout in #eng-oncall and #announcements.

Owners:

* Standard owner: Observability (Allison Grant)
* Dashboard coordination: Sergio Costa
* Incident process coordination: Rafael Mendes

h2. FAQ

h3. What if multiple categories apply?

Pick the category that best explains the primary failure mechanism. Use *incident.contributing_factors* and the postmortem narrative to capture additional causes.

h3. Is “severity” part of this standard?

Severity is managed by the Incident Response process and has separate definitions. This standard focuses on metadata used for ownership + reporting.

h3. Are security incidents included?

Security incidents follow the Security IR process. When appropriate, Security may populate shared fields like *incident.region* and *incident.impacted_surface* for reporting consistency, but the incident record system-of-record remains Security IR.

h3. What if the incident is only internal tooling?

Set:

* incident.impacted_surface = internal.ops_tooling
* incident.customer_tier = internal_only

…and choose the category that matches the failure mechanism.
